t: Find the Median of the Uniqueness Array — Binary Search + Sliding Window
o: There are T = n(n+1)/2 subarrays; we need the k-th smallest distinct-count where k = ⌈T/2⌉ (the smaller middle). Distinct-counts range in [1, n] and the count of subarrays with ≤ v distinct elements is monotone in v, so binary search on v. Counting subarrays with at most v distinct elements is a classic sliding window with a frequency map. n ≤ 1e5 → O(n log n). For [1,2,3]: T=6, k=3; three subarrays have ≤1 distinct, so the answer is 1.
k: Median-of-multiset reduces to k-th smallest via monotone counting predicate.

a.n: Approach 1: Binary search on answer + at-most-v sliding window
a.i: For candidate v, slide a window maintaining distinct counts; the number of windows with ≤ v distinct is Σ (right − left + 1). Find the smallest v whose count ≥ k.
s: countLE(v): two pointers with a frequency map; shrink while distinct > v.
Return first v with countLE(v) ≥ k.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def medianOfUniquenessArray(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        T = n * (n + 1) // 2
        k = (T + 1) // 2
        def countLE(v):
            cnt = defaultdict(int)
            distinct = left = 0
            total = 0
            for right, x in enumerate(nums):
                if cnt[x] == 0: distinct += 1
                cnt[x] += 1
                while distinct > v:
                    cnt[nums[left]] -= 1
                    if cnt[nums[left]] == 0: distinct -= 1
                    left += 1
                total += right - left + 1
            return total
        lo, hi = 1, n
        while lo < hi:
            mid = (lo + hi) // 2
            if countLE(mid) >= k: hi = mid
            else: lo = mid + 1
        return lo

a.t: O(n log n) — log n binary-search rounds, each an O(n) sliding window

a.n: Approach 2: Parallel binary search over all candidates at once
a.i: Instead of binary searching one v at a time, run a single sliding-window pass while binary-searching inside: for each right endpoint, binary search the minimal window length with ≤ v distinct. This yields the same complexity with a different constant profile and generalizes when the predicate isn't two-pointer friendly.
s: For each right endpoint, binary search the smallest left with distinct(left..right) ≤ v.
Combine with the outer selection of the k-th value via nested binary search.

w: Careful with T overflowing 32-bit (n = 1e5 → ~5·10^9). The subtle definition detail: for even-length uniqueness arrays take the smaller middle, i.e., k = ⌈T/2⌉. Follow-up: exact median for streams, or counting subarrays with exactly v distinct (atMost(v) − atMost(v−1)).
